blocks.x: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation applied to Property & Casualty. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

P&C economics live in two moments: pricing the risk before the event and handling the claim after it. Both are decision factories — rate against exposure and catastrophe models, settle against policy language and fraud signals — and both reward carriers whose document and data machinery is industrialized.

items: FNOL, estimates, medical and police files arrive as documents; triage takes days and leakage hides in the queue.
Telematics and GLM pricing outrun validation and filing capacity; model risk documentation is rebuilt under exam.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Hyperautomation & Systems Integration, Decision Intelligence Systems, Process & Task Mining from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower, wired into the unit's workflows (FNOL and claims triage, Estimate review and leakage control, Commercial risk surveying) on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — Rate filing regimes among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Agents that execute the work: tool-using, policy-bounded, and fully logged for audit.
Agents operated as one fleet: roles, queues, budgets and audit trails.
Decision paths that run in milliseconds, with policy checks and full logging.
Documents classified/extracted; straight-through for clean claims with audit replay (triage in minutes)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: entity-link analytics scoring claims and applications against ring patterns (organized-fraud capture up 25%+). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
